criteria.SC1_totp_replay: PASS. Migration 0134 adds user_mfa.last_totp_step (bigint, nullable) with a .down.sql; readback confirms the column and the enrollment burn (step 59626338). RED-first at the service level with a fixed clock (TestTOTPCodeIsBurnedAfterFirstUse). Live: the SAME code answered 200 then 401 with a body byte-identical to a wrong code's, the burn mark advanced 59626338 -> 59626339, the code stayed refused 29 s later inside the ±1 skew window, and the next step's code answered 200. An unpaced replay burst gave 7x401 then 5x429 on the shipped 10/min per-IP limiter (the window already held 3 requests), so a replay counts exactly like a wrong code. Recovery codes unaffected: one completed the challenge in the same window a replay had just been refused in.
criteria.SC2_admin_mfa: PASS. AdminUser.mfa_enabled is additive in the core PR and true only for the account that had enrolled (bob true; ada, mona, cleo, dara false). DELETE /admin/users/{id}/mfa answered 204 with 0 bytes; user_mfa and mfa_recovery_codes rows for the target both dropped to 0; the audit envelope carried admin.user.mfa_reset success, resource_id = the target, changes [{mfa_enabled true -> false}] and no prose; the notice reached the target naming an administrator and carrying no secret. Wrong actors, once each: anonymous 401, ordinary user 403, moderator 403, wrong ADMIN password 403 — and after all four refusals the target's user_mfa.enabled was still true and no notice had been sent. Self-reset allowed and audited, and the acting session survived it, with the SELF-worded notice (not the admin one). Chromium: the detail read 'Two-factor = On' with the control and its password field, the copy stating 'signs out every device' and 'never see their secret'; the removal flipped the fact to Off with 'Removed. bob can sign in with their password…'; on an account with no second factor the control was DISABLED with 'This account has no second factor.' beside it and no password field at all.
criteria.SC3_removal_revokes_sessions: PASS. DELETE /mfa/totp answered 204; the removing session kept answering 200 on /auth/me and the other device's access token answered 401 within one request (session-bound). The account was mailed the self-worded notice. The admin reset takes the same path: both of the target's sessions 401'd. In Chromium the second context was signed out — /settings/security went from the signed-in card to 'Sign in to manage security settings' on the next navigation.
criteria.SC4_smtp_probe: PASS. probeSMTP now performs EHLO -> STARTTLS (when offered) -> AUTH (when credentials are configured) -> QUIT within the existing 3 s budget and sends no message (asserted: the probe issued QUIT and never MAIL/RCPT/DATA). Per-variant, live: plain no-auth relay = smtp ok, instance ok; STARTTLS with an untrusted certificate = smtp down, instance degraded, 'the relay advertises STARTTLS but the encrypted session could not be established … x509: certificate signed by unknown authority'; credentials against a relay that offers no AUTH = down/degraded, 'SMTP_USERNAME is set but this relay offers no AUTH, so every send fails closed…'; relay down = down/degraded, 'the mail relay could not be reached … connection refused'; something answering that is not a relay = down/degraded, 'something answered on that port but it did not greet as an SMTP relay…'. MAIL_ENABLED=false keeps not_configured, and not_configured still never degrades (instance stayed ok). The first two variants are the exact states A05 measured as smtp: ok while every send failed; a real password-reset send against the STARTTLS one failed with the identical x509 error, so probe and mailer agree.
criteria.SC5_verification_resend: PASS. POST /api/v1/auth/verify-email/resend, unauthenticated, takes {email}. With the gate effective, registration answered 202 {"status":"verification_pending"} and login answered 403 email_verification_required. The resend answered 202 with a ZERO-byte body for a known unverified address, an unknown address and an already-verified one, and cmp confirmed the three bodies byte-identical. A resend inside the 60 s per-address send cooldown answered 202 and put nothing in the mailbox (Mailpit 4 -> 4); past the cooldown a message arrived and its token confirmed (204) and unblocked login (200). An unpaced burst gave 7x202 then 7x429 on the shared 10/min per-IP limiter. The audit row is auth.email_verify.request with no actor_id, no reason and no address anywhere in the ledger (0 matches for the address across 30 rows). Chromium: the sign-in screen offered 'Resend verification email' after a held EMAIL attempt and the click delivered a real message (Mailpit 9 -> 10), with the conditional confirmation 'If that address has an unconfirmed account here…' and no delivery claim; a held USERNAME attempt showed the same gate copy and NO resend control; the signup 'Check your email' panel offered it too.
criteria.SC6_mail_not_configured: PASS. With MAIL_ENABLED=false, POST /auth/me/email-change answered 503 with the stable code mail_not_configured and the full sentence ('…so it cannot deliver the confirmation this change needs. The token goes to the new address and nowhere else… Set MAIL_ENABLED=true with SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT and SMTP_FROM, then restart the api') — not scrubbed. The resend answered the same code. Nothing was started: GET /auth/me/email-change reported {"pending":false} and the unused email_change_requests table stayed at 0. With mail wired the same request answered 202, so the refusal is the mail path and not the change. The three bare boot-capability 503s A17/A27 measured are typed too, with a control asserting a BARE 503 still loses its message.
criteria.SC7_oauth_documented: PASS. env/production.env.example and env/staging.env.example document OAUTH_PROVIDERS and the per-provider OAUTH_<NAME>_{ISSUER,CLIENT_ID,CLIENT_SECRET,SCOPES}, the callback URL to register (<PUBLIC_BASE_URL>/api/v1/auth/oauth/<name>/callback), that PUBLIC_BASE_URL becomes required and https-in-production once the list is non-empty, that an incomplete provider is a boot failure, and that the block is UNPROVEN (AUTH-04). tests_updated_because_they_pinned_the_de: TestImportResolverRequestValidation, TestChannelSyncBootDisabled503 and TestAutoCaptionBootDisabled503 each asserted error code service_unavailable — which is what the central 5xx scrubber produced AFTER throwing the operator sentence away. They now pin the stable code and assert that the message names the variable to set.

TestTOTPEnrollVerifyAndMFALogin and three httpapi MFA tests reused the ENROLLMENT code on the login challenge, which the burn now forbids. They take the next step's code; a challengeCode helper states why once.
defects_found_and_fixed: The email-change RESEND was as dead as the request with no mail path, and was not in the ruling: it is refused with the same typed code.

MailNotConfiguredError's single sentence ('there is nothing to test') was written for the admin mail probe and would have been wrong on a user-facing refusal. It now carries the consequence, and the admin probe's message is byte-identical to before.
findings_recorded_not_fixed: Compose has no wildcard env passthrough, so only OAUTH_PROVIDERS itself reaches the api container from an env file; each provider's four variables must ALSO be named in the api service's environment map in vidra-core/docker-compose.yml. Setting them in the env file alone makes the api see the provider list, find it incomplete, and refuse to boot. Documented in both templates rather than changed, because provider names are operator-chosen and no wildcard is expressible.

The stale-ISR path for the email card (mailEnabled true in a 60 s-old snapshot, server answering 503) is covered by a component test, not by a browser observation: reproducing it needs a mail-off restart inside the revalidate window, which is a race rather than a measurement.

The STARTTLS SUCCESS path (a trusted CA) is proven by unit test only. Go on darwin reads the system keychain and ignores SSL_CERT_FILE, so making a self-signed relay trusted needs a containerised Linux core, exactly as the A05 evidence records. The FAILURE path was proven live.
OIDC remains unexercised. The env-template block is documentation of the configuration surface, not evidence that a login through it works.

attempts_and_corrections: The first probe rewrite kept smtpGreeter (a server that writes 220 and hangs up) behind TestSystemStatusSMTPProbe, which then failed — correctly, because a relay that greets and hangs up cannot deliver. That test now asserts `down` and a real mini-relay carries the ok case.
The admin instance-settings PATCH takes a JSON boolean, not the string "true" (422 'must be a boolean'), which cost one attempt before the verification gate could be turned on.
sqlc typed the burn parameter as *int64 because the column is nullable; the ::bigint cast on sqlc.arg('step') makes it a plain int64 and keeps the call sites honest.
